examples.trans: The bread rings are very tasty.

Всем = to everyone (dative). Core Russian pron meaning 'all; everyone' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And you know the main thing? Nobody cares.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'егда').

examples.trans: She's offended. She's always like that.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'валить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to overwhelm, fail'.

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет завалить без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to overwhelm without a reason.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

meanings.note: Also a flat number in an address. Common feminine noun meaning 'flat, apartment' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Do you remember the toilet in the communal flat?

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'sausage', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Осторожно, ты пронзил меня своей колбасой!
examples.trans: Careful, you impaled me with your sausage!

examples.text: Обидишь Настю, я из тебя колбасу сделаю.
examples.trans: If you hurt Nastya, I will turn you into sausage.

meanings.note: In business, sport or an election. From German 'Konkurrent' / Latin 'concurrens' ('running together', rival).

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Кричать на + accusative. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to shout', paired with 'крикнуть'.

examples.text: Не надо кричать. Хорошо, я буду сегодня.
examples.trans: There's no need to shout. All right, I'll be there tonight.

meanings.note: Comparative of хорошо. Core Russian adv meaning 'better' in everyday speech.
+ infinitive. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Надо + infinitive. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'рушить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to disturb / break'.

examples.text: Добрый день, позвольте нарушить вашу тихую беседу.
examples.trans: Good afternoon, allow me to interrupt your quiet conversation.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и нарушить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to disturb on time.

meanings.note: Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Habitually or in progress. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'купать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to buy', paired with 'купить'.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нцип'). Common masculine noun meaning 'principle' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
